related_resources.reason: Broad biographical source for Jordan’s engineering, academic career, and contributions in algebra, topology, and analysis.
A near-contemporary memorial providing depth on Jordan’s life and scientific community.

A modern, detailed derivation of canonical blocks and generalized eigenvectors; explains numerical instability.
Jordan’s original 1875 essay on geometry in n dimensions, relevant to the angles-between-subspaces account.

Modern statement and historical context for composition factors and Jordan–Hölder.
Detailed account of Jordan’s 1878 theorem and differential-equation motivation.
Statement and background of the plane separation theorem.

Background for the total-variation example in Jordan’s analysis work.
Overview and further pointers for the mathematician and similarly named concepts.
